hints: Focus on what type of hydrolysis this is, alkaline with NaOH is not the same as acidic with dilute acid.
Split the ester CH3CO2CH2C2H5 into its acid part CH3CO and its alcohol part OCH2C2H5 to see what each becomes.
Remember that a carboxylic acid made in NaOH solution is immediately neutralised to its sodium salt, while the alcohol stays as a neutral molecule.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the ester**

This is a lovely straightforward ester. The left side comes from the acid and the right side comes from the alcohol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \text{ is propyl ethanoate}$$

**Apply alkaline hydrolysis**

With aqueous NaOH we get saponification. The ester breaks at the C-O bond to give a carboxylate salt plus an alcohol, not a free acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOR} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{ROH}$$

**Identify the two products**

Here R is $\text{CH}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$, so we make sodium ethanoate and propan-1-ol.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2^-\text{Na}^+ + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

options.A: Correct. This is sodium ethanoate, the carboxylate salt formed when the CH3CO part of the ester is hydrolysed and then neutralised by NaOH. This is exactly what alkaline hydrolysis gives.
options.B: Not correct. CH3CO2H is ethanoic acid, which is formed by acid hydrolysis with dilute HCl or H2SO4. In NaOH solution any acid formed would be neutralised at once to the salt, so free acid cannot survive.
options.C: Not correct. The alcohol product is neutral propan-1-ol, C2H5CH2OH, not the alkoxide ion C2H5CH2O- Na+. Alkoxides are destroyed by water and only form with reactive metals like Na, not with aqueous NaOH.
options.D: Not correct. This suggests the acid part was C2H5CH2CO2, but the acid part of this ester is CH3CO2 from ethanoate. You have mixed up the two sides of the ester, taking the alcohol chain as the acid chain.
